subtopics.title: India's Partnerships: Vietnam, New Zealand and SAARC
subtopics.summary: India and Vietnam raised their ties to an enhanced Comprehensive Strategic Partnership after a state visit by To Lam, with a target of USD 25 billion bilateral trade by 2030. India and New Zealand signed a free trade agreement that eliminates duties on Indian exports to New Zealand. The SAARC currency swap framework, launched by the RBI in 2012, offers short-term liquidity support to member nations.
facts: India and Vietnam elevated ties to an enhanced Comprehensive Strategic Partnership after a state visit by To Lam
Target: USD 25 billion bilateral trade by 2030
Vietnam formally joined the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative
Joint Vision Statement for 2030 seeks deeper defence cooperation and joint development of advanced defence platforms
India extended a USD 500 million defence line of credit to Vietnam
India-New Zealand FTA eliminates duties on Indian exports to New Zealand (100% duty elimination)
India gives access to 70.03% of tariff lines and keeps 29.97% under exclusion
New Zealand to invest USD 20 billion over 15 years
SAARC currency swap: central banks exchange domestic currencies at a predetermined rate and reverse the swap at the same rate
SAARC swap tenure is 3 months, extendable twice; launched by RBI in 2012

subtopics.title: ASEAN: Structure, Principles and Forums
subtopics.summary: ASEAN was formed on 8 August 1967 and is headquartered in Jakarta, with 11 members now including Timor-Leste. It works on three principles: non-interference, consensual decision-making and centrality in regional matters, and its Charter took effect in 2008. The group runs several forums and economic pacts, and India's Act East Policy places ASEAN at the centre of its Indo-Pacific vision.
facts: Formed on 8 August 1967 at Bangkok, Thailand; headquarters in Jakarta, Indonesia
11 members, including Timor-Leste (2025)
Core aims: accelerate economic and social progress, promote regional peace and stability, foster collaboration, cooperate with global organisations
Principles: non-interference in internal affairs, consensual decision-making, and maintaining centrality in regional matters
ASEAN Charter took effect on 15 December 2008; it is legally binding and registered with the UN Secretariat
East Asia Summit created in 2005 as a leaders-level forum with a varied agenda
ASEAN Free Trade Area (AFTA) established in 1992 to create a single market
ASEAN Regional Forum (ARF) established in 1994 for political and security dialogue
ASEAN Economic Community formed in 2015 to facilitate free flow of goods, services, investments, capital and labour
RCEP concluded in 2019, covering 30% of the world's population

subtopics.title: Global Issues: Thucydides Trap, Ebola and Ecocide
subtopics.summary: The Thucydides Trap describes the heightened risk of conflict when a rising power challenges an established power, and it is often applied to China and the United States. WHO declared an Ebola outbreak in DR Congo a Public Health Emergency of International Concern, linked to the Bundibugyo strain. Ecocide refers to unlawful or reckless acts that cause severe environmental damage, and it is not currently recognised under the Rome Statute.
facts: The Thucydides Trap idea originates from Thucydides' account of the Peloponnesian War between Athens and Sparta
Core argument: growth of Athenian power and the fear it caused in Sparta made conflict increasingly inevitable
The trap describes a heightened risk of conflict when a rising power challenges an established power
Critics argue the idea oversimplifies by implying conflict is unavoidable; diplomacy and economic interdependence can prevent escalation
WHO declared the DR Congo Ebola outbreak a PHEIC, linked to the Bundibugyo strain in the Ituri region
Under the IHR 2005, a PHEIC is a public health risk of international disease spread requiring coordinated global response
Ebola is a zoonotic, severe and fatal viral disease, first identified in 1976
Ecocide: unlawful or reckless acts committed knowing they are likely to cause severe, widespread or long-term environmental damage
Ecocide is not currently recognised under the Rome Statute; India has not signed the Rome Statute and is not bound by ICC jurisdiction
Recognised international crimes under the Rome Statute: genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes and crime of aggression

subtopics.title: Governance, Citizenship and Parliament
subtopics.summary: Draft Citizenship Rules amendments tighten declaration and passport-surrender norms for applicants from Pakistan, Afghanistan and Bangladesh, and India does not allow dual citizenship. A privilege notice moved in Rajya Sabha shows how MPs can allege a breach of parliamentary privilege. The Model Code of Conduct regulates elections, and the Supreme Court's One Case One Data initiative aims to integrate court data.
facts: Citizenship is covered under Part II (Articles 5 to 11) of the Constitution and is a Union List subject
India does not allow dual citizenship; acquiring foreign citizenship leads to automatic termination of Indian citizenship
Applicants must declare whether they hold a valid or expired passport from Pakistan, Afghanistan or Bangladesh
Under the draft rules, a foreign passport must be surrendered within 15 days
Citizenship Act, 1955 lists five modes of acquisition: birth, descent, registration, naturalisation and incorporation of territory
A privilege notice is a formal mechanism to allege breach of parliamentary privilege or contempt of the House; it is derived from Article 105
Privilege notices are submitted under Lok Sabha Rule 222 or Rajya Sabha Rule 187; the Speaker or Chairman decides whether to allow discussion or refer it to the Privileges Committee
Model Code of Conduct: non-statutory guidelines issued by the Election Commission to ensure a free, fair and level-playing field, with no unfair advantage to the ruling party
One Case One Data integrates case data from the Supreme Court, High Courts, district courts and taluka courts into one platform; Su Sahay is an AI chatbot on the Supreme Court website

subtopics.title: Economy, Agriculture and Employment
subtopics.summary: The RBI's Economic Capital Framework governs how it provides for risks and transfers surplus to the government, and the RBI Board approved a record transfer for FY 2025-26. The Index of Eight Core Industries and the Manufacturing PMI track industrial activity, with the PMI at 54.7 in April 2026. The Mission for Cotton Productivity aims at self-sufficiency in cotton by 2030-31, and the Centre raised the sugarcane Fair and Remunerative Price for the 2026-27 season.
facts: Economic Capital Framework (introduced in 2019) governs how the RBI provides for financial risks and transfers surplus to the Government of India
Surplus is transferred to the government only after Contingency Risk Buffer targets are met
RBI Board approved a record 2.86 lakh crore surplus transfer for FY 2025-26
Section 47 of the RBI Act, 1934 mandates that RBI profits be sent to the Centre
RBI surplus transfer typically averages around 0.5% of GDP
Eight core industries: coal, crude oil, natural gas, refinery products, fertilisers, steel, cement and electricity (base year 2011-12)
Index of Eight Core Industries grew 1.7% in April 2026; core industries carry a 40.27% weight in the Index of Industrial Production
Manufacturing PMI rose to 54.7 in April 2026; a PMI above 50 signals expansion, compiled by S&P Global
Mission for Cotton Productivity (Kapas Kanti), 2026-27 to 2030-31, aims to make India self-sufficient in cotton
Bt cotton is the only GM crop approved by GEAC for commercial cultivation in India

quizzes.passage: Southeast Asia is home to a regional grouping that has become central to how countries in the region manage their relations with one another and with major outside powers. Its members have long preferred a cautious style of diplomacy, in which governments avoid commenting on or interfering in each other's domestic affairs. Leaders and ministers meet through a network of regional forums that cover trade, politics and security, and several of these meetings now include partners from outside the region. The group has also tried to deepen economic ties, aiming to make trade, investment and the movement of people easier across national borders. Its record is not without difficulty. Member states hold different views on the rivalry between China and the United States, a dispute over a busy sea route has remained unresolved for years, and the group has been criticised for its limited response to a political crisis inside one of its member states. For India, the region has a special importance. New Delhi has built deep political, economic and security ties with the grouping over many years, and its own regional outreach policy places the grouping at the heart of its approach to the wider Indo-Pacific. The group's ability to act together will shape how much influence it can exercise in the years ahead.

quizzes.passage: The Reserve Bank of India earns income from its operations, and every year it decides how much of that income to keep and how much to pass on to the central government. The rules for these decisions are set out in a framework known as the Economic Capital Framework, which tells the bank how to provide for financial risks and how to transfer its surplus. A surplus is the net income left after total expenditure is deducted from total income. The bank earns this income from buying and selling bonds in the market, from the interest it receives on bonds it holds, and from returns on its foreign currency assets. To guard against unexpected losses, such as falls in the value of securities or the effects of changes in interest rates, the bank maintains a contingency buffer. The surplus is handed over to the government only after this buffer has reached its target level. The bank's board has recently approved a record transfer to the government, and the framework itself has been reviewed by expert committees over time. Analysts see these transfers as helping the government with its finances, reducing its borrowing needs and supporting its spending on infrastructure.
